agent.name: Flag
agent.strategy: Bull flag: pole, quiet drift, breakout
agent.description: Well-formed bull flags across the universe: forming flags with their trigger and stop, and breakouts on volume with the trade attached.

context.label: Well-formed
context.value: flag vol <= 70% of pole, pullback <= 40%, 5-8 sessions

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 22% pole · 8-session flag · 37% pullback on 45% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This flag shows mixed signals: the 37% retracement is shallow (textbook flags hold 33-50%), but the volume compression at 45% of pole volume is weak—strong flags typically see 30% or less, suggesting weak accumulation rather than coiled strength. A clean breakout would require a decisive close above $118.41 on expanding volume (ideally 1.5x+ average); if it instead drifts sideways above the trigger or fails to hold it on volume, the flag is likely breaking down given HAE's already-negative momentum today.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 20% pole · 5-session flag · 30% pullback on 43% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This flag is messy: the pullback already retraced 70% of the pole's gain (to $80.27), which is deeper than the textbook 25–50%, and volume during the flag construction was weak relative to the pole, both red flags for follow-through. A breakout above $82.90 on volume exceeding the pole's average would confirm the pattern, but given that flags-in-formation have a poor breakout rate, a close below $80.27 or a failed retest of $82.90 would kill it and likely signal momentum exhaustion rather than a setup.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 35% pole · 7-session flag · 31% pullback on 65% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This flag shows weak structure: the pullback consumed 69% of the pole's gains (closing at $36.86 vs. $36.79 support), leaving minimal room for a clean breakout, and the 7-session consolidation is short for conviction. Confirmation requires a decisive close above $39.42 on expanding volume—anything less is likely continued decay toward $36 or below, which historically is the more probable outcome for forming flags.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 19% pole · 5-session flag · 33% pullback on 61% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This is a messy flag at best: the 33% retracement is shallow for a genuine consolidation, and forming flags statistically break down more often than they break up, especially on declining volume into the flag. Confirmation would require a decisive break above $65.70 on volume expansion matching the pole's strength; failure to hold $65.00 or a retest of the $64.96 low would signal the flag is deteriorating into a failed pattern.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 16% pole · 5-session flag · 32% pullback on 64% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This flag setup shows mixed signals: the 5% retracement is textbook shallow, but the volume compression to 64% of pole volume is weaker than ideal—flags typically consolidate on 40-50% volume for clean breakouts. Confirmation would require a decisive close above $43.38 on expansion volume; a break below $41.44 with no reversal would invalidate it, though statistically forming flags have poor predictive value and breakdowns are more common than breakouts.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 29% pole · 5-session flag · 39% pullback on 62% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This flag shows mixed signals—the pullback to $42.75 is appropriately shallow (39% retracement), but the volume compression at 62% of pole volume is weak for a reversal pattern, and flags mid-formation historically fail more often than they succeed. Confirmation requires a decisive close above $45.04 on volume expansion; breakdown below $42.75 or another lower low in the flag would kill it. Without seeing the flag form to completion *and* breach the trigger with conviction, treating this as a high-probability setup would be premature.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 26% pole · 5-session flag · 31% pullback on 67% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This is a borderline flag with weak construction: the pullback consumed 31% of the pole on only 67% of volume, suggesting weak selling pressure rather than orderly consolidation—classic conditions for breakdown. Confirmation would require a decisive close above $86.56 on volume expansion (not just a touch of $83.32), while any close below $81.00 likely kills it; the real risk is a slow bleed lower that never triggers, which is how most forming flags fail.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 35% pole · 5-session flag · 38% pullback on 68% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This flag shows mixed signals: the pullback to $8.94 is textbook (38% retrace, low volume), but the pole's 35% gain is modest and today's -4% close suggests weakening conviction rather than consolidation before a breakout. Confirmation would require a clean break above $9.40 on expanding volume *without* retesting the flag midline; a close below $8.94 or another failed probe near $9.40 kills it—and statistically, the latter is more likely given the pole lacked dominant strength to begin with.
